newsitem.title: USA: Judge nullifies Citicorp benefits contract.
newsitem.headline: Judge nullifies Citicorp benefits contract.

text.p: A New York State Supreme Court judge on Tuesday nullifed a contract that called for Citicorp's Citibank unit to take a big role in electronic distribution of benefits in the state, an attorney for the plaintiffs said.
The attorney, Gerald Goldman, said the court found there were violations ot the New York state's bidding laws.
Citicorp officials were not immediately available for comment.
Plaintiffs in the lawsuit included the Check Cashers Association of New York, a trade group for companies that cash checks for a fee for individuals who generally do not have bank accounts.

In a recent interview, Stephen Wolf, chairman of the National Check Cashers Association and also treasurer of Syosset, N.Y.-based Pay-O-Matic Corp PAYO.OB, said check cashers have been happy with an electronic system in use for years in New York but have "major issues" with the system planned by Citibank.
In the interview on February 14, Wolf said Citibank's plan to allow benefit recipients to draw cash from automated teller machines and supermarkets was "totally inadequate."
"We don't believe that the system is going to answer the needs of the people who live in the inner city where the dense welfare population is," he said.
